nodes.label: GUS Projekt
nodes.desc: Investigating codon-optimised GUS (coGUS) sense-strand toxicity in E. coli. When cloning coGUS into pGGZ001 (GoldenGate Level 0 acceptor, Spec resistance), colony PCR consistently shows inserts only in antisense orientation. This project systematically maps the toxic regions, identifies the responsible reading frames, and tests suppression strategies (terminators, RNase E sites, tRNA supplementation, Agrobacterium bypass). All inserts are ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001 unless stated otherwise.

nodes.label: Suppression via Triple-Terminator and RNase E recognition motif
nodes.desc: Strategy to prevent readthrough transcription from upstream promoters in pGGZ001 that may drive expression of the toxic coGUS insert. A triple rrnB terminator and/or RNase E cleavage site is placed upstream of the insert to degrade any readthrough mRNA before it reaches the coding region. If successful, sense-orientation clones should become recoverable.

nodes.label: Transformation in Agrobacterium
nodes.desc: Bypass strategy: transform GUS constructs directly into Agrobacterium tumefaciens (GV3101) instead of E. coli. Agrobacterium uses different codon usage and transcription machinery, so the polyleucine toxicity observed in E. coli may not occur. If sense clones are recoverable in Agrobacterium, this confirms the toxicity is E. coli-specific and provides a practical workaround for plant transformation experiments.

nodes.label: Rescue by supplying more t-RNA?
nodes.desc: Hypothesis: the toxicity of coGUS sense-strand expression is caused by ribosome stalling on polyleucine stretches (CTC repeats in RF2), which depletes tRNA-Leu pools and triggers a growth arrest. If true, co-expressing extra tRNA-Leu from a constitutive promoter should rescue growth and allow sense-orientation clones to survive. The tRNA-Leu gene is cloned downstream of the insert to supplement the cellular tRNA pool.

nodes.label: STOP codons in 3rd 5th of coGUS (nt 725-1086)
nodes.desc: The 3rd fifth of coGUS (~362 nt, nt 725-1086) shows the strongest antisense bias of all fragments and only grows in antisense orientation (confirmed by colony PCR of @pDC042). This sub-project introduces early STOP codons via silent mutations into specific reading frames (RF1, RF2, or both) at positions ~120 nt and ~240 nt within the fragment. By selectively terminating translation in individual reading frames, we can identify which reading frame produces the toxic peptide. RF3 already contains natural stop codons throughout.

nodes.label: Testing of predicted RBS in coGUS with npmA in pDC050
nodes.desc: RBS (ribosome binding site) predictions were generated by denovodna.com for each coGUS fifth. The predictions correlated well with the sense/antisense bias: every fifth that grew only in antisense had a predicted RBS in reading frame 2 (the toxic polyleucine frame). To experimentally validate RBS strength, each predicted RBS sequence was cloned upstream of npmA in pDC050 (a pGGZ001 derivative with triple terminator). NpmA expression from the predicted RBS was read out as Kan resistance. RESULT: RBS strength did not correlate with sense/antisense bias — approach scrapped. E.g., @pDC052 (RBS2, from 5th2 which shows sense clones) gave >100 colonies, while @pDC051 (RBS from 5th1, no sense clones) gave 0.

nodes.label: GUS parts experiments
nodes.desc: Systematic fragmentation of coGUS into progressively smaller pieces (halves, thirds, fifths) to map the toxic region(s). Each fragment is PCR-amplified and ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001. Colony PCR determines sense vs. antisense orientation. Frameshift variants (+1 nt, +2 nt at 5' end via primer extension) test whether toxicity depends on the native reading frame or persists across all three frames. Temperature experiments (37 C vs. RT) test whether toxicity is growth-rate dependent.

nodes.label: NpmA
nodes.desc: NpmA (aminoglycoside N1-methyltransferase) was the initial resistance marker. NpmA modifies 16S rRNA at A1408, conferring Kan resistance. However, NpmA was TOO efficient: even a few protein molecules per cell modify enough ribosomes for full resistance. Impossible to distinguish readthrough levels between @pDC005, @pDC006, @pDC007, @pDC008. CONCLUSION: replaced with NptII series (@pDC013 ff., less efficient, requires more protein). Important finding: in pGGZ001, NO antisense transcription occurs — otherwise antisense-oriented npmA inserts would have produced Kan-resistant colonies.

nodes.label: nptii
nodes.desc: NptII (neomycin phosphotransferase II) replaced NpmA as resistance marker because it requires higher expression levels for kanamycin resistance, making it a better reporter for readthrough transcription strength. Workflow: (1) transform on Spectinomycin plates (selects for pGGZ001 backbone, not insert orientation), (2) colony PCR to verify insert presence and orientation, (3) inoculate confirmed colonies into liquid cultures with kanamycin gradient (0-50 ug/ml) to quantify NptII expression from readthrough. Various suppression elements (single/triple terminator, RNase E site, tRNA-Leu) are tested in combination.

nodes.label: sug/GUS
nodes.desc: Full-length coGUS (sense = GUS, antisense = SUG) with various suppression element combinations in pGGZ001. The ultimate test: can any strategy make full-length coGUS clonable in sense? Tested: @pDC031 (no suppression), @pDC009 (Ter+RNE), @pDC010 (Ter+SUG antisense ctrl), @pDC020 (tRNA), @pDC021 (Ter+tRNA), @pDC026 (Ter3+RNE), @pDC027 (Ter3+tRNA), @pDC077 (Ter2+eRNE). RESULT: ALL unclonable in sense. Even minimal readthrough transcription of coGUS is lethal to E. coli.

nodes.label: EXPERIMENT
nodes.desc: RBS-npmA constructs in pDC050 (pGGZ001 with integrated triple terminator upstream of ccdB). Each predicted RBS from a coGUS fifth is fused to npmA via primer and ligated into SmaI-opened pDC050. The npmA reading frame is NOT in frame with ccdB, ensuring that any NpmA produced comes exclusively from translation initiated at the predicted RBS. Transformed on Kan plates to select for functional RBS-driven NpmA expression.

nodes.label: controls
nodes.desc: Control constructs: identical RBS-npmA inserts in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator) instead of pDC050. Controls: @pDC059 for @pDC051, @pDC060 for @pDC052, @pDC061 for @pDC053, @pDC062 for @pDC054, @pDC063 for @pDC055, @pDC064 for @pDC056, @pDC065 for @pDC057, @pDC066 for @pDC058. If colonies grow on Kan for pGGZ001 controls but not pDC050 constructs, the triple terminator effectively blocks readthrough.

nodes.label: halfs
nodes.desc: coGUS split at nt 967 into two halves (~967 nt and ~925 nt). Each half tested in all 3 reading frames: native (RF1), +1 nt frameshift (RF2), +2 nt frameshift (RF3) via 5' primer extension. All 6 constructs show 100% antisense except @pDC028 (1st half, RF1) which produced 2 sense out of 10 colonies. @pDC033 (1st half, RF2) showed extremely poor growth — even worse than RF1 — suggesting RF2 is particularly toxic, consistent with the polyleucine hypothesis.

nodes.label: thirds
nodes.desc: coGUS digested with SspI + EcoRV to generate 3 fragments of roughly equal size (~600 nt each). Each third cloned separately into pGGZ001 in native reading frame. All three thirds grew exclusively in antisense orientation, confirming that the toxicity is distributed across the entire gene and not confined to a single region. The reading frame shifts caused by restriction sites were not further explored at this stage.

nodes.label: fifth
nodes.desc: coGUS split into 5 equal fragments of ~362 nt each. Each fifth tested in all 3 reading frames (native RF1, +1 nt = RF2, +2 nt = RF3) by primer extension. Additional experiments at room temperature (RT, ~22 C) vs. 37 C to test growth-rate dependence. This is the highest-resolution mapping of toxic regions. Key finding: the 3rd fifth (nt 725-1086) shows the strongest antisense bias across all reading frames, and the 2nd fifth (nt 363-742) shows the most variable results with some reading frames allowing sense clones.

nodes.label: fifth 1
nodes.desc: First fifth of coGUS (nt 1-362). Contains the N-terminal region of GUS. RF1 (native): 2s/14as, slight sense tolerance (@pDC040). RF2 (+1 nt): 1s/15as, nearly all antisense (@pDC088). RF3 (+2 nt): 7s/8as, almost 50/50 (@pDC099). The strong bias in RF1 and RF2 but not RF3 indicates a reading-frame-specific toxic peptide in this region.

nodes.label: fifth 2
nodes.desc: Second fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742). Most variable results of all fifths. RF1: 8s/1as at 37C (@pDC089), 10s/10as at RT — surprisingly sense-tolerant. RF2: 3s/5as at 37C (@pDC090), 9s/15as at RT. RF3: 6s/9as at 37C (@pDC041), 8s/13as at RT. Reverse primer frameshifts (@pDC104, @pDC105, @pDC106, @pDC107, @pDC109, @pDC110) tested at RT. This fifth contains the predicted RBS2 which showed highest npmA expression in @pDC052.

nodes.label: fifth 3
nodes.desc: Third fifth of coGUS (nt 725-1086). THE most toxic fragment — strongest antisense bias across all reading frames. RF1: 1s/13as (@PDC091). RF2: 0s/15as, 100% antisense (@pDC042). RF3: 0s/11as (@pDC100). This region contains a predicted RBS in RF2 that initiates translation of a polyleucine stretch (CTC codon repeats). The combination of functional RBS + polyleucine coding sequence in RF2 is the leading candidate for the toxicity mechanism. Target for STOP codon mutagenesis: @pDC070, @pDC072, @pDC073, @pDC074, @pDC080, @pDC081, @pDC082.

nodes.label: fifth 4
nodes.desc: Fourth fifth of coGUS (nt 1087-1449). Strong antisense bias in RF1 (0s/14as, @pDC043) and RF2 (0s/13as, @pDC092), but RF3 shows mixed results (6s/8as, @pDC101). The RF3 tolerance suggests that the toxic peptide(s) in this region are specific to RF1 and RF2 reading frames. @pDC043 was also used for the Agrobacterium transformation test (@pDC043A) and tRNA rescue experiment (@pDC078).

nodes.label: fifth 5
nodes.desc: Fifth fifth of coGUS (nt 1450-1812, C-terminal region). RF1 (native): 9s/7as, nearly 50/50 (@pDC044). RF2: 0s/15as, 100% antisense (@pDC093). RF3: 0s/11as (@pDC102). The stark contrast between RF1 (tolerated) and RF2/RF3 (lethal) is the clearest example of reading-frame-dependent toxicity in the entire dataset.

elements.label: pDC117
elements.desc: Triple terminator (Ter3) + RNase E recognition site upstream of full-length coGUS in pGGZ001. Maximum suppression configuration combining both transcriptional termination and mRNA degradation elements. Tests whether blocking readthrough AND degrading any escaped transcripts is sufficient to allow sense-orientation cloning of coGUS.

elements.label: pDC108
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator upstream of full-length coGUS in pGGZ001. Minimal suppression element — tests whether a single terminator alone is sufficient to block readthrough transcription and allow sense clones. Compared to pDC117 (Ter3+RNE) and pDC031 (no suppression) to evaluate terminator contribution.

elements.label: pDC043A
elements.desc: @pDC043 (4th fifth of coGUS, nt 1087-1449, RF1) electroporated into Agrobacterium tumefaciens GV3101. In E. coli, @pDC043 shows 0s/14as. If Agrobacterium yields sense clones, the toxicity is confirmed as E. coli-specific, likely due to differences in codon usage, RBS recognition, or tRNA pools between the two species.

elements.label: pDC078
elements.desc: Full-length coGUS co-expressed with a constitutive tRNA-Leu gene in pGGZ001. Hypothesis: polyleucine translation from RF2 depletes cellular tRNA-Leu-CAG, causing ribosome stalling and toxicity. Supplementing tRNA-Leu should prevent the depletion bottleneck. If sense clones are recovered, this confirms tRNA depletion as the toxicity mechanism. Test construct: @pDC043. See also NptII+tRNA variants: @pDC022, @pDC023, @pDC025.

elements.label: oDC067
elements.desc: Primer for amplifying the E. coli tRNA-Leu (CAG anticodon) gene including its native promoter. Used to generate the tRNA-Leu cassette for co-expression in pDC078 and other tRNA rescue constructs (pDC022, pDC023, pDC025, pDC027).

elements.label: pDC043
elements.desc: GUS 4th fifth (nt 1087-1449) in pGGZ001, used as the test construct for tRNA rescue experiments. Chosen because it shows 0/14 sense colonies in E. coli (strong antisense bias) yet is small enough to reduce cloning complications. Serves as the baseline for comparing with pDC078 (+ tRNA-Leu).

elements.label: pDC070
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS (nt 725-1086) with STOP codons in both RF1 and RF2 at positions ~120 nt and ~240 nt. RF3 already contains natural stops. This is the maximum suppression variant — if sense clones appear, at least one of RF1/RF2 was responsible for toxicity. Compared to single-RF knockouts (@pDC072, @pDC073) to identify the causal frame. See also @pDC042 (unmodified 3rd fifth).

elements.label: pDC072
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS with an early STOP codon in RF1 only, at approximately nt 120 of the 362 nt fragment. RF2 and RF3 remain unmodified. If sense clones appear with only RF1 blocked, RF1 encodes the toxic peptide. If toxicity persists, RF2 (polyleucine) is the likely culprit.

elements.label: pDC073
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS with an early STOP codon in RF2 only, at ~nt 120 of 362. RF1 and RF3 remain unmodified. RF2 contains the predicted polyleucine-encoding region with a functional RBS — directly tests whether blocking the polyleucine peptide rescues sense-orientation growth. Compare: @pDC072 (RF1 only), @pDC074 (RF1+RF2), @pDC042 (unmodified).

elements.label: pDC074
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS with early STOP codons in both RF1 AND RF2 at approximately nt 120. Only RF3 (which already has natural stops) remains translatable. Same as pDC070 but with stops only at early positions. Compared to pDC072 (RF1 only) and pDC073 (RF2 only) to determine if both frames contribute additively to toxicity.

elements.label: pDC080
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS with 2 STOP codons in RF1 at positions ~120 nt and ~240 nt. Double stops provide more complete translational termination than single stops (pDC072), in case the first stop is read through by near-cognate suppressor tRNAs. RF2 remains fully open.

elements.label: pDC081
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS with 2 STOP codons in RF2 at positions ~120 nt and ~240 nt. Double stops ensure complete termination of the polyleucine peptide even if the first stop is suppressed. RF1 remains fully open. This is the strongest single-frame test for the polyleucine toxicity hypothesis.

elements.label: pDC082
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS with 2 late STOP codons in BOTH RF1 and RF2 at position ~240 nt only (no early stop at 120). Tests whether late termination alone is sufficient — if toxicity requires translation of >240 nt of the toxic peptide, late stops should rescue. If toxicity occurs within the first 240 nt, this construct will still be toxic.

elements.label: pDC051
elements.desc: Predicted RBS from 5th1 (nt 1-362, RF2) fused to npmA in pDC050 (triple terminator vector). Result: 0 colonies on Kan. This RBS is from a fifth that shows almost no sense clones (2s/14as in RF1), consistent with low RBS activity. However, the lack of correlation with other fifths led to the approach being scrapped.

elements.label: pDC052
elements.desc: Predicted RBS from 5th2 (nt 363-742, RF2) fused to npmA in pDC050. Result: ~100 colonies on Kan — by far the strongest RBS tested. However, 5th2 actually shows some sense clones (6s/9as in RF3), which contradicts the expectation that strong RBS = more toxicity = fewer sense clones. This discrepancy was the key reason the RBS approach was abandoned.

elements.label: pDC053
elements.desc: Predicted RBS from 5th3 (nt 725-1086, RF2) fused to npmA in pDC050. Result: 15 colonies on Kan. Moderate RBS strength, but 5th3 is THE most toxic fifth (0s/15as in RF2). If RBS strength alone explained toxicity, this should have been the strongest RBS — it wasn't. Suggests toxicity depends on what is translated (polyleucine), not just translation initiation strength.

elements.label: pDC054
elements.desc: Predicted RBS from 5th4 (nt 1087-1449, first predicted site) fused to npmA in pDC050. Result: 0 colonies on Kan. Consistent with 5th4 showing no sense clones in RF1/RF2 (0s/14as and 0s/13as respectively).

elements.label: pDC055
elements.desc: Predicted RBS from 5th4 (nt 1087-1449, second predicted site) fused to npmA in pDC050. Result: 7 colonies on Kan. Weak RBS activity, consistent with the moderate toxicity of this region. Two RBS predictions existed for 5th4; this one is slightly active while the other (pDC054) gave 0 colonies.

elements.label: pDC056
elements.desc: Predicted RBS from 5th5 (nt 1450-1812) fused to npmA in pDC050. Result: 20 colonies on Kan. Moderate RBS activity. 5th5 shows mixed sense/antisense in RF1 (9s/7as) but 100% antisense in RF2/RF3 — the RBS strength does not explain why RF1 is tolerated.

elements.label: pDC057
elements.desc: Negative control 1: random 67 nt sequence (no predicted RBS) fused to npmA in pDC050. Result: 0 colonies on Kan. Confirms that the triple terminator in pDC050 effectively blocks background transcription and that colonies in other constructs are genuinely RBS-driven.

elements.label: pDC058
elements.desc: Negative control 2: random 73 nt sequence (no predicted RBS) fused to npmA in pDC050. Result: 1 colony on Kan. Near-zero background, consistent with control 1 (pDC057). The single colony may be a spontaneous Kan-resistant mutant or a very rare suppressor event.

elements.label: pDC059
elements.desc: RBS1-npmA in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator). Control for pDC051. Any colonies on Kan would indicate that upstream readthrough transcription in pGGZ001 can drive npmA expression via this RBS, independent of the triple terminator.

elements.label: pDC060
elements.desc: RBS2-npmA in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator). Control for pDC052. Since RBS2 was the strongest RBS (100 colonies in pDC050), this control tests whether it also functions in pGGZ001 context where readthrough transcription should be present.

elements.label: pDC061
elements.desc: RBS3-npmA in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator). Control for pDC053.

elements.label: pDC062
elements.desc: RBS4-npmA in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator). Control for pDC054.

elements.label: pDC063
elements.desc: RBS5-npmA in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator). Control for pDC055.

elements.label: pDC064
elements.desc: RBS6-npmA in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator). Control for pDC056.

elements.label: pDC065
elements.desc: Random sequence control 1 (67 nt) in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator). Control for pDC057. Tests whether background readthrough in pGGZ001 alone (without RBS) can produce enough npmA for Kan resistance.

elements.label: pDC066
elements.desc: Random sequence control 2 (73 nt) in pGGZ001 (no triple terminator). Control for pDC058.

elements.label: pDC028
elements.desc: 1st half of coGUS (nt 1-967) in native reading frame (RF1). Insert amplified by PCR with primers oJF1533 + oJF1536 on coGUS template, ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001. Result: 2 sense / 8 antisense colonies. This is the ONLY halves construct that yielded any sense clones, suggesting the 1st half in RF1 has slightly lower toxicity than all other half/frame combinations.

elements.label: pDC029
elements.desc: 2nd half of coGUS (nt 968-1892) in native reading frame (RF1). Insert amplified by PCR with primers oJF1534 + oJF1535 on coGUS template, ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001. Result: 0 sense / 13 antisense — 100% antisense. The 2nd half is fully toxic in RF1.

elements.label: pDC033
elements.desc: 1st half of coGUS (nt 1-967) with +1 nt frameshift (RF2). Insert amplified with primer oDC046 (adds 1 extra nt at 5') + oJF1536 on coGUS template, ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001. Result: 0 sense / 14 antisense. VERY poor growth overall — no bacteria survived on backup plate or in liquid culture. RF2 is even MORE toxic than the native RF1 (pDC028 had 2 sense), strongly supporting that polyleucine stretches in RF2 cause the most severe growth defect.

elements.label: pDC034
elements.desc: 1st half of coGUS (nt 1-967) with +2 nt frameshift (RF3). Insert amplified with primer oDC047 (adds 2 extra nt at 5') + oJF1536 on coGUS template, ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001. Result: 0 sense / 12 antisense — 100% antisense. RF3 is also toxic for the 1st half, but growth was better than pDC033 (RF2).

elements.label: pDC035
elements.desc: 2nd half of coGUS (nt 968-1892) with +1 nt frameshift (RF2). Insert amplified with primer oDC048 (adds 1 extra nt at 5') + oJF1536 on coGUS template, ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001. Result: 0 sense / 16 antisense — 100% antisense.

elements.label: pDC036
elements.desc: 2nd half of coGUS (nt 968-1892) with +2 nt frameshift (RF3). Insert amplified with primer oDC049 (adds 2 extra nt at 5') + oJF1536 on coGUS template, ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001. Result: 0 sense / 15 antisense — 100% antisense.

elements.label: pDC037
elements.desc: 1st third of coGUS (nt 1-749) in reading frame 1. Generated by SspI + EcoRV digest of coGUS and ligation into pGGZ001. Result: 1 sense / 9 antisense. Similar to pDC028 (1st half) — the N-terminal region has slight sense tolerance in RF1.

elements.label: pDC038
elements.desc: 2nd third of coGUS (nt 750-1270) in reading frame 2 (shifted by restriction site). Generated by SspI + EcoRV digest. Result: 0 sense / 13 antisense — 100% antisense. This region overlaps with the highly toxic 3rd fifth (nt 725-1086) and part of the 4th fifth.

elements.label: pDC039
elements.desc: 3rd third of coGUS (nt 1271-1812) in reading frame 2 (shifted by restriction site). Generated by SspI + EcoRV digest. Result: 0 sense / 10 antisense — 100% antisense. Covers the C-terminal region including parts of 4th and 5th fifths.

elements.label: pDC040
elements.desc: 1st fifth of coGUS (nt 1-362) in native reading frame (RF1). PCR-amplified and ligated into SmaI-opened pGGZ001. Result: 2 sense / 14 antisense. Corresponding RBS prediction (pDC051) gave 0 colonies — no functional RBS detected in this region, yet antisense bias persists, suggesting toxicity mechanism may not require internal RBS.

elements.label: pDC041
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in RF3 (+2 nt frameshift). Result at 37 C: 6 sense / 9 antisense. Result at RT: 8 sense / 13 antisense. RF3 shows moderate sense tolerance at both temperatures, more sense clones than RF2 but fewer than RF1 (pDC089).

elements.label: pDC042
elements.desc: Originally the 3rd fifth (nt 725-1086) construct at the fifths level. Moved to its own sub-node (fifth 3) for better organization since this fragment became the focus of extensive follow-up experiments (STOP codon mutagenesis). See pDC042 under fifth 3 node.

elements.label: pDC043
elements.desc: 4th fifth of coGUS (nt 1087-1449) in native reading frame (RF1). Result: 0 sense / 14 antisense — 100% antisense. This construct was also repurposed for the Agrobacterium test (pDC043A) and tRNA rescue experiment (pDC078) due to its strong, consistent antisense bias.

elements.label: pDC044
elements.desc: 5th fifth of coGUS (nt 1450-1812) in native reading frame (RF1). Result: 9s/7as — nearly 50/50, the LEAST toxic construct in the entire fifths series. The C-terminal region of GUS in its native frame does not produce a lethal peptide, contrasting sharply with RF2 (@pDC093: 0s/15as) and RF3 (@pDC102: 0s/11as).

elements.label: pDC088
elements.desc: 1st fifth of coGUS (nt 1-362) in RF2 (+1 nt frameshift). Result: 1 sense / 15 antisense. Stronger antisense bias than RF1 (pDC040: 2s/14as), consistent with RF2 being more toxic due to polyleucine-encoding codons.

elements.label: pDC099
elements.desc: 1st fifth of coGUS (nt 1-362) in RF3 (+2 nt frameshift). Result: 7 sense / 8 antisense — nearly 50/50. RF3 is clearly non-toxic for this region, while RF1 and RF2 are toxic. This pattern (RF3 tolerance) is also seen in the 4th and 5th fifths.

elements.label: pDC089
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in native reading frame (RF1). Result at 37C: 8s/1as — MOSTLY SENSE, a striking exception. Result at RT: 10s/10as — 50/50. This is the only fifth where RF1 is predominantly sense at 37C. Compare @pDC090 (RF2: 3s/5as) and @pDC041 (RF3: 6s/9as). Reverse-primer variants: @pDC106, @pDC107.

elements.label: pDC090
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in RF2 (+1 nt frameshift). Result at 37 C: 3 sense / 5 antisense. Result at RT: 9 sense / 15 antisense. More antisense-biased than RF1 (pDC089) but less than the 3rd fifth. Temperature effect: more sense clones at RT, suggesting the toxic peptide is less harmful at slower growth rates.

elements.label: PDC091
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS (nt 725-1086) in RF1 (native). Result: 1 sense / 13 antisense. Even RF1 (the GUS reading frame) is highly toxic in this region. The single sense colony may be a suppressor mutant or a colony that incorporated a truncated/mutated insert.

elements.label: pDC042
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS (nt 725-1086) in RF2 (+1 nt frameshift). Result: 0s/15as — 100% antisense, the strongest bias in the entire dataset. This reading frame contains the predicted polyleucine-encoding RBS. Colony PCR confirmed all 15 colonies have antisense inserts. This result is the primary evidence for the polyleucine toxicity hypothesis and motivated the STOP codon mutagenesis series (@pDC070, @pDC072, @pDC073, @pDC074, @pDC080, @pDC081, @pDC082). Compare @PDC091 (RF1) and @pDC100 (RF3).

elements.label: pDC100
elements.desc: 3rd fifth of coGUS (nt 725-1086) in RF3 (+2 nt frameshift). Result: 0 sense / 11 antisense — 100% antisense. Unlike other fifths where RF3 shows some tolerance, RF3 is also completely toxic in the 3rd fifth. This suggests multiple toxic reading frames overlap in this region, making it the most problematic segment of coGUS.

elements.label: pDC092
elements.desc: 4th fifth of coGUS (nt 1087-1449) in RF2 (+1 nt frameshift). Result: 0 sense / 13 antisense — 100% antisense. RF2 is fully toxic, same as RF1 (pDC043: 0s/14as). Only RF3 (pDC101) shows any sense tolerance in this region.

elements.label: pDC101
elements.desc: 4th fifth of coGUS (nt 1087-1449) in RF3 (+2 nt frameshift). Result: 6 sense / 8 antisense — mixed, with moderate sense tolerance. RF3 is the only non-lethal reading frame in this region, consistent with the pattern seen in 1st and 5th fifths. Suggests RF3 rarely encodes toxic peptides across the coGUS sequence.

elements.label: pDC093
elements.desc: 5th fifth of coGUS (nt 1450-1812) in RF2 (+1 nt frameshift). Result: 0 sense / 15 antisense — 100% antisense. Dramatic contrast to RF1 (pDC044: 9s/7as). The 5th fifth C-terminal region is only toxic when read in RF2, strongly implicating the polyleucine codon pattern that exists in RF2 throughout the coGUS gene.

elements.label: pDC102
elements.desc: 5th fifth of coGUS (nt 1450-1812) in RF3 (+2 nt frameshift). Result: 0 sense / 11 antisense — 100% antisense. Like RF2, RF3 is also fully toxic in this region. Only the native RF1 (pDC044: 9s/7as) is tolerated, making the 5th fifth unique in that the native frame is the LEAST toxic.

elements.label: pDC104
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in RF3, with reverse primer adding +1 nt frameshift. Tested at RT only. Result: 5 sense / 7 antisense. Part of a series (pDC104-110) testing whether frameshift at the 3' end (via reverse primer) rather than the 5' end changes the reading frame throughout the fragment and alters toxicity patterns.

elements.label: pDC105
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in RF3, reverse primer +2 nt frameshift. Tested at RT. Result: mixed (exact counts not recorded). Exploring whether 3'-end frameshifts produce different toxicity profiles than 5'-end frameshifts for the same reading frame.

elements.label: pDC106
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in RF1, reverse primer +1 nt frameshift. Tested at RT. Result: 0 sense / 20 antisense — 100% antisense with 20 colonies checked. Striking contrast to the forward-primer RF1 (pDC089: 8s/1as at 37 C). The 3'-end frameshift apparently disrupts something that makes the forward-RF1 tolerated.

elements.label: pDC107
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in RF1, reverse primer +2 nt frameshift. Tested at RT. Result: 10 sense / 10 antisense — exactly 50/50. Non-toxic. Together with pDC106 (0s/20as), this shows that the exact 3'-end context matters: +1 nt makes it lethal, +2 nt makes it neutral.

elements.label: pDC109
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in RF2, reverse primer +1 nt frameshift. Tested at RT. Result: 11 sense / 4 antisense — predominantly SENSE. Unexpected: most RF2 constructs are highly toxic, but this 3'-frameshift variant is well-tolerated. Suggests the C-terminal portion of the RF2 peptide contributes to toxicity.

elements.label: pDC110
elements.desc: 2nd fifth of coGUS (nt 363-742) in RF2, reverse primer +2 nt frameshift. Tested at RT. Result: 11 sense / 14 antisense — mixed, slightly biased toward antisense. Less tolerant than pDC109 (+1 nt rev) but much more tolerant than forward-primer RF2 (pDC090: 3s/5as at 37 C). The reverse-primer frameshifts consistently alter the toxicity profile of this fifth.

elements.label: pDC013
elements.desc: NptII resistance gene alone (no suppression elements) in pGGZ001. Baseline control for the NptII suppression series. Transformed on Spectinomycin plates (backbone selection), then colony PCR to confirm insert, then inoculated into Kanamycin gradient (0-50 ug/ml) to quantify NptII expression from readthrough transcription. Any Kan resistance indicates readthrough-driven NptII translation.

elements.label: pDC014
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + NptII + RNase E recognition site in pGGZ001. Dual suppression: terminator blocks transcription, RNase E site degrades any readthrough mRNA. Should show lower Kan resistance than pDC013 (NptII alone) and pDC015 (Ter+NptII) if both elements contribute independently.

elements.label: pDC015
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + NptII in pGGZ001. Tests terminator-only suppression without RNase E element. Compared to pDC013 (no suppression) and pDC014 (Ter+NptII+RNE) to isolate the terminator's contribution to reducing readthrough.

elements.label: pDC016
elements.desc: NptII + RNase E recognition site in pGGZ001 (no terminator). Tests RNase E-only suppression. The RNase E site should trigger mRNA cleavage by cellular RNase E, reducing the half-life of readthrough transcripts. Compared to pDC013 (no suppression) to quantify RNase E contribution alone.

elements.label: pDC022
elements.desc: NptII + tRNA-Leu cassette in pGGZ001 (no terminator). Tests whether tRNA-Leu supplementation alone affects NptII expression/readthrough. Not directly related to toxicity suppression but controls for any effect of the tRNA gene on transcription or translation in the region.

elements.label: pDC023
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + NptII + tRNA-Leu in pGGZ001. Combines terminator with tRNA-Leu supplementation. Tests combined effect on NptII readthrough expression.

elements.label: pDC024
elements.desc: Triple rrnB terminator (Ter3) + NptII in pGGZ001. Triple terminator should be more effective than single terminator (pDC015) at blocking readthrough. This is the same triple terminator design used in pDC050 for the RBS experiments.

elements.label: pDC025
elements.desc: Triple rrnB terminator (Ter3) + NptII + tRNA-Leu in pGGZ001. Maximum suppression combination with NptII: triple terminator + tRNA supplementation. Should show the lowest Kan resistance if both elements work synergistically.

elements.label: pDC032
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + ectopic RNase E recognition site + NptII in pGGZ001. The RNase E site is placed at an 'ectopic' position (between terminator and NptII rather than after NptII) to test whether placement of the RNase E cleavage site relative to the gene affects suppression efficiency.

elements.label: pDC009
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + full-length coGUS (sense) + RNase E recognition site in pGGZ001. Tests whether Ter+RNE combination allows sense-orientation cloning of full-length GUS. Result: unclonable — no sense colonies recovered. The suppression elements are insufficient against full-length GUS toxicity.

elements.label: pDC010
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + full-length coGUS in ANTISENSE orientation (SUG) + RNase E recognition site in pGGZ001. Antisense control for pDC009. Should be clonable since the antisense strand does not encode the toxic peptides. Confirms that suppression elements don't interfere with cloning per se.

elements.label: pDC020
elements.desc: Full-length coGUS (sense) + tRNA-Leu cassette in pGGZ001 (no terminator). Tests whether tRNA-Leu supplementation alone can rescue GUS sense toxicity. Result: unclonable. tRNA supplementation without blocking readthrough transcription is not sufficient.

elements.label: pDC021
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + full-length coGUS (sense) + tRNA-Leu in pGGZ001. Combines terminator and tRNA supplementation. Result: unclonable. Even dual suppression (Ter + tRNA) is not enough for full-length GUS.

elements.label: pDC026
elements.desc: Triple rrnB terminator (Ter3) + full-length coGUS (sense) + RNase E recognition site in pGGZ001. Strongest transcription-blocking combination tested with full-length GUS. Result: unclonable. Even triple terminator + RNase E cannot overcome GUS toxicity.

elements.label: pDC027
elements.desc: Triple rrnB terminator (Ter3) + full-length coGUS (sense) + tRNA-Leu in pGGZ001. Combines the strongest terminator with tRNA supplementation. Result: unclonable. This was the most aggressive suppression strategy tested and it still failed, suggesting that even trace readthrough transcription produces enough toxic peptide to kill the cell.

elements.label: pDC031
elements.desc: Full-length coGUS (sense) alone in pGGZ001 — no suppression elements. Negative control baseline. Result: unclonable, as expected. Confirms the fundamental observation that coGUS in sense orientation is lethal in E. coli without any suppression.

elements.label: pDC077
elements.desc: Double rrnB terminator (Ter2) + ectopic RNase E recognition site + full-length coGUS (sense) in pGGZ001. Tests an intermediate terminator strength (2x instead of 1x or 3x) with ectopic RNase E placement. Result: unclonable. Confirms the pattern: no suppression combination works for full-length GUS.

elements.label: pDC005
elements.desc: NpmA resistance gene alone in pGGZ001. Baseline control for NpmA suppression series. Transformed on Kanamycin to test whether readthrough transcription in pGGZ001 drives enough NpmA expression for resistance. Result: too efficient — even minimal NpmA expression confers full Kan resistance, making quantitative comparison impossible.

elements.label: pDC006
elements.desc: NpmA + RNase E recognition site in pGGZ001. Tests whether RNase E-mediated mRNA degradation reduces NpmA expression enough to see a difference on Kan plates. Likely still too efficient due to NpmA's catalytic mechanism (single enzyme modifies multiple ribosomes).

elements.label: pDC007
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + NpmA in pGGZ001. Tests terminator suppression of NpmA readthrough expression. Key finding from this construct series: on Kan plates, ALL colonies had sense-orientation inserts, confirming that no antisense transcription occurs in pGGZ001 — if it did, antisense-oriented npmA would also produce protein and confer resistance.

elements.label: pDC008
elements.desc: Single rrnB terminator + NpmA + RNase E recognition site in pGGZ001. Maximum suppression for NpmA series. Despite both suppression elements, NpmA's extreme efficiency (A1408 methylation is catalytic) still likely confers resistance. This observation motivated the switch to NptII (pDC013-032) as a less efficient, more quantitative reporter.
